newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Southern Africa urged to take advantage of peace.
newsitem.headline: Southern Africa urged to take advantage of peace.

text.p: Southern Africa should take advantage of the relative peace it is enjoying for the first time in centuries to foster growth and lift the region out of poverty and under-development, a regional conference heard on Thursday.

Cyril Ramaphosa, executive deputy chairman of South Africa's New Investments Limited, warned that without substantial economic growth and job creation, the moderate advances the region has made in human development would be short-lived.

"Southern Africa as a whole has made a remarkable political recovery, which makes possible for the first time an economic and social recovery to lift the region out of poverty and under- development," he said.
"The relative political stability within and between the countries of southern Africa means that the energies and resources of the people can be directed into productive economic activity.
"The figurative swords of the past can now become ploughshares," Ramaphosa told the Southern African Trade and Investment Summit which ended in Harare on Thursday.

He pointed to such peace milestones in the region as the end of apartheid rule in South Africa and of its destabilisation policies against its neighbours and to the peace process in oil and diamond-rich Angola after almost two decades of civil war.
But he said the region needed to register far higher levels of economic growth and human development than it had achieved so far if is to recover fully from decades of civil strife.

"As has been vividly illustrated at this summit, increased investment - both from within the region and beyond its borders - is key to any substantial economic growth. So too are efforts which empower national economies to process their own raw materials and market them competitively," he said.

He said southern Africa should make sustainable use of its natural wealth, much of which still lies untapped, and which had already established it in the world as an important area of agricultural and mineral production.

"I believe governments in this part of the continent must create opportunities...they must set up enabling mechanisms to make people come into their own and investment is the key to any substantial growth..I believe we must make southern Africa matter more to the world," he said.
